population: HCV genotype 1 (the palm/thumb-site non-nucleoside inhibitors are genotype-1-restricted)
note: HCV grows in no ordinary lab animal, so the non-nucleoside NS5B inhibitors (dasabuvir, filibuvir, tegobuvir, setrobuvir, lomibuvir, beclabuvir, ABT-072, radalbuvir, TMC647055, CDI-31244) went to patients on the genotype-1 subgenomic replicon; the replicon called the antiviral effect and the resistance sites but not whether an add-on to peginterferon would cure, and only dasabuvir, inside a three-DAA regimen, reached approval.
label: NS5B non-nucleoside inhibitors

engagement.model: HCV genotype 1 subgenomic replicon (Huh-7), with and without human serum
engagement.note: Filibuvir inhibited the genotype 1b-Con1 replicon at 75 nM and 22 of 23 clinical-isolate chimeras at a mean 59 nM; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Filibuvir inhibits GT1 replicon at 59-75 nM
engagement.quote: It is a potent and selective inhibitor, with a mean 50% inhibitory concentration of 0.019 μM against genotype 1 polymerases and a mean 50% effective concentration (EC50) of 0.075 μM against the genotype 1b-Con1 replicon.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed record); 'microM' and 'EC(50)' in the PubMed rendering written as μM and EC50 here.
engagement.judgement: Opener for the replicon track at the first peer-reviewed member characterisation I could verify (filibuvir, Mar 2009); tegobuvir and HCV-796 used the replicon earlier but HCV-796 is not a member and the tegobuvir primary was not verified in budget. The replicon is a cell-culture system, not patient tissue; ex_vivo is the nearest enum.

engagement.model: HCV genotype 1 subgenomic replicon (Huh-7), with and without human serum
engagement.note: Across 8 non-nucleoside polymerase inhibitors, protein-shifted replicon EC50 with day-3 plasma trough predicted the 3-day monotherapy HCV RNA decline in genotype 1 patients.
engagement.short: Replicon EC50 predicted monotherapy RNA decline
engagement.quote: The VK model was successfully used to predict VL decreases in 3-day monotherapy for NNPolIs based on the EC(50,PS) and the day 3 C(min).
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level: the 8 NNPolIs are named only in the body (Europe PMC full text not served, PMC not fetched in budget), so which members (filibuvir, tegobuvir, setrobuvir, lomibuvir, dasabuvir, ABT-072 all had 3-day monotherapy data by 2011) were in the set is unverified; the size of the fit is not recorded.
engagement.judgement: Viral load is the replicon's own read-out (RNA replication), so this is engagement at proximal tier, class-level. Roche authors put replicon EC50,PS and patient VL declines side by side for the class, so comparison_stated is true. The same paper scored the sibling protease-inhibitor class a miss (liver-to-plasma ratio needed), which is the NS3/4A tile's business, not this one's. product_in_model null because the member list of the 8 NNPolIs was not read. Subscripts flattened in the quote as PubMed renders them.
engagement.magnitude_basis: log10 HCV RNA decline at day 3, predicted vs observed (fold error is in the paper body, not read)

engagement.model: HCV genotype 1 subgenomic replicon (Huh-7), with and without human serum
engagement.note: Dasabuvir: replicon EC50 1.8-7.7 nM (13-fold shift in 40% plasma); 3-day monotherapy in genotype 1 patients cut HCV RNA 1.4 log10.
engagement.short: Dasabuvir monotherapy cut HCV RNA 1.4 log10
engagement.quote: Dasabuvir doses between 25 and 100 mg per day reduced viral load by 1.4 log10 at steady-state with AUCs between 2.2 to 8.6 µg•hr/mL.
engagement.confidence_note: FDA Medical Review read in the bundle text; model side is the Kati 2015 abstract (doi:10.1128/AAC.04619-14, epub 2014-12-22). The monotherapy study NCT00696904 posted no registry results. The MedR's 25-100 mg/day dose range is lower than the 400-800 mg BID dasabuvir monotherapy doses reported elsewhere; quoted as written.
engagement.judgement: Member-specific strengthening of the 2012 class entry: I paired the AbbVie replicon paper with the FDA's summary of the dasabuvir phase 1b monotherapy study, so comparison_stated is false. Direction only: a 1.4 log10 decline is the modest NNI monotherapy effect, not the 3-4 log10 of the NS3/4A and NS5A partners, which the replicon potency ranking also gave (the FDA ClinPharm review notes ABT-450 had the greatest monotherapy potency). Year 2014 is the FDA review and the Kati epub, both December 2014.
engagement.magnitude_basis: log10 HCV RNA decline on 3-day monotherapy vs replicon EC50 rank
engagement.reason: Replicon potency matched patient RNA decline

engagement.model: HCV-infected chimpanzee, 14-day NNI monotherapy (A-837093, dasabuvir's Abbott palm-I sibling)
engagement.note: Two HCV-infected chimpanzees on A-837093 30 mg/kg BID: maximum HCV RNA drop 1.4 (GT1a) and 2.5 (GT1b) log10 within 2 days; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.quote: Maximum viral load reductions of 1.4 and 2.5 log(10) copies RNA/ml for genotype 1a- and 1b-infected chimpanzees, respectively, were observed within 2 days after the initiation of treatment.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed record PMID 17908950; PMC2167986 not read). The checker's lead names this 'Long 2007'; the first author is Chen C-M (Long MA is a co-author). 'log(10)' as PubMed renders it. Epub 2007-10-01, print Dec 2007 (AAC 51(12):4290-6).
engagement.judgement: Opener for the chimpanzee track at the only member-class chimpanzee study found: the animals were dosed with A-837093, an Abbott benzothiadiazine palm-I sibling of dasabuvir, not a member, so product_in_model false. The chimpanzee is the one immunocompetent animal that carries HCV; it reads plasma HCV RNA, the proximal readout. No FDA review in the bundle cites it (model_filed false).

engagement.model: HCV-infected chimpanzee, 14-day NNI monotherapy (A-837093, dasabuvir's Abbott palm-I sibling)
engagement.note: Dasabuvir 3-day monotherapy cut genotype 1 patients' HCV RNA 0.95-1.08 log10 (ABT-072: 1.07-1.57), matching the chimpanzee's 1.4 log10 GT1a drop on the sibling.
engagement.short: Patient NNI monotherapy drop matched chimp
engagement.confidence_note: The quote is the ABT-333 400 mg BID row of Reddy's Table 1 (compound, dose, N total/1a/1b, day-3 Cmin µg/ml, observed and predicted log10 VL decrease), cells joined with '|', read from the PMC HTML rendering; the paper has no prose sentence giving the dasabuvir number (the 800 mg BID row reads −0.95, ABT-072 rows −1.07 to −1.57). If a prose sentence is required this entry falls to untested. The FDA MedR line 978 ('1.4 log10', 25-100 mg/day) is the reviewer error the checker flagged and is not used.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: the chimpanzee's maximum decline on the sibling (1.4 log10 GT1a, 2.5 GT1b, within 2 days) against Reddy's Table 1 day-3 monotherapy declines for the two Abbott members (ABT-333 −1.08/−0.95 at 400/800 mg BID; ABT-072 −1.07 to −1.57), so comparison_stated false. Same in direction and within 2x on the GT1a animal; the GT1b animal over-called by about 2.5x, recorded in magnitude_basis. Dated to Reddy's 2012 publication, the earliest tier-1 record of the dasabuvir monotherapy numbers I could verify; the 2009 AASLD abstracts that first reported them are not an admissible tier. Dose differs (30 mg/kg BID chimpanzee vs 400-800 mg BID patients) and the model stated no exposure target, so no dose entry on this track.
engagement.magnitude_basis: maximum log10 HCV RNA decline on NNI monotherapy: chimpanzee GT1a 1.4 (sibling A-837093, day 2) vs genotype 1 patients 0.95-1.08 (dasabuvir, day 3); the GT1b chimpanzee's 2.5 log10 is off by 2-5x
engagement.reason: Chimp sibling drop matched patient monotherapy

dose.model: Viral-kinetic PK/PD model: day-3 plasma trough over protein-shifted replicon EC50
dose.note: The exposure target (day-3 Cmin relative to protein-shifted replicon EC50) predicted NNI monotherapy viral-load declines; each extra log10 needed a 10-fold higher trough.
dose.quote: VK model simulations suggested that achieving additional log(10) VL decreases greater than one required 10-fold increases in the C(min). NNPolI and PI data further supported this result.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; which 8 NNPolIs and the predicted-vs-observed fold error are in the body, not read. Not checked whether the Viekira Pak NDA cites a viral-kinetic model (model_filed null).
dose.judgement: A separate track from the replicon: the viral-kinetic model is a different system (in silico, built on Neumann-type kinetics) making a different prediction (how much viral-load decline a given plasma trough buys), per this run's track-identity rule. Scored same because the stated exposure target was reached in the 3-day monotherapy studies and the model's effect size held for the NNI class; no tolerability margin is part of this model (margin_stated null). The toxic end of the dose window is scored on the animal toxicology track below.
dose.magnitude_basis: log10 HCV RNA decline at day 3, predicted vs observed

dose.note: Animals tolerated 10-120x the clinical dasabuvir exposure with no target organ; patients were dosed to 250 mg BID with no dasabuvir-attributed toxicity.
dose.quote: Overall, systemic exposures in nonclinical studies ranged from approximately 10 to 120-fold higher than clinical exposures. Therefore, the nonclinical toxicology program is considered to be adequate to predict toxicity in the clinical setting.
dose.confidence_note: FDA Pharmacology Review executive summary read in the bundle text; the patient side (no exposure-safety signal for dasabuvir) is the FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review of the same NDA. Dasabuvir is one of three DAAs in the regimen, so component attribution of clinical tolerability is inferential.
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the animal package stated a tolerated exposure far above the effective one (no target organ at 10-120x), and patients reached the 250 mg BID target without that toxicity, so dose is same with margin_stated true. The FDA reviewer places animal exposure multiples against clinical exposure and concludes the package predicts the clinic, so comparison_stated is true. The failed members (filibuvir, tegobuvir, setrobuvir, lomibuvir) were not stopped for missed exposure targets as far as I could verify; tegobuvir's 2007 phase 1 QT signal is press-release only and its preclinical prediction was not found, so it is not scored.
dose.magnitude_basis: animal NOAEL exposure multiple over clinical AUC
dose.reason: Stated animal margin held in patients

efficacy.model: HCV genotype 1 subgenomic replicon (Huh-7), with and without human serum
efficacy.note: The replicon selected M423T, a single thumb-site substitution giving 761-fold filibuvir resistance, forecasting a low barrier to resistance; no patient outcome yet.
efficacy.quote: An in vitro resistance study of PF-00868554 identified M423T as the predominant resistance mutation, resulting in a 761-fold reduction in susceptibility to PF-00868554
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed record); the quoted clause is the first half of a longer sentence.
efficacy.judgement: Opener on the replicon track: the model's two efficacy predictions for the class are antiviral activity in genotype 1 and a single-substitution resistance barrier. Same source as the engagement opener.

efficacy.model: HCV genotype 1 subgenomic replicon (Huh-7), with and without human serum
efficacy.note: Dasabuvir, potent in the genotype 1 replicon, delivered SVR24 of 83-100% inside three-DAA regimens; dropping it raised virologic failure in genotype 1a.
efficacy.quote: The rates of sustained virologic response across all treatment subgroups ranged from 83 to 100%.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Kowdley 2014; the dasabuvir-specific contribution is in the FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review of the same study (M11-652): removal of ABT-333 or ABT-267 from 3-DAA + RBV raised virologic failure in genotype 1a treatment-experienced subjects to 19.2-50% versus 4%. Model side is the Kati 2015 abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Primary endpoint (SVR24) of a dasabuvir-containing regimen, so endpoint_role primary; the replicon predicted genotype 1 activity and the trial confirmed it, with the FDA's component-removal arms isolating dasabuvir's share. Paired by me (model paper and trial paper), so comparison_stated is false. Both 2014 entries share a year: the filibuvir registry results (2014-01-27) actually preceded the dasabuvir model paper (Dec 2014), but the rule that one drug's contra beats another's same on the same track makes the track contra either way, and placing the match first is the only lint-valid way to keep both on record. The later SAPPHIRE-I phase 3 (NCT01716585, registry results 2015-01-06, primary endpoint SVR12; its NEJM paper's DOI was not verified in budget, so none is cited) is listed in patient_trials and changes no status.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: SVR with vs without dasabuvir in the 3-DAA regimen

patient_trials.quote: The rates of sustained virologic response across all treatment subgroups ranged from 83 to 100%.

efficacy.model: HCV genotype 1 subgenomic replicon (Huh-7), with and without human serum
efficacy.note: Filibuvir, potent in the replicon, added to peginterferon/ribavirin raised on-treatment response but not SVR (41.7/39.6% vs 45.8% placebo) because of relapse.
efficacy.short: Filibuvir add-on failed SVR despite replicon potency
efficacy.quote: Filibuvir plus pegIFN/ribavirin did not improve the percentage of patients achieving SVR compared with administration of pegIFN/ribavirin alone.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 24927607; Annals of Hepatology 13(4):364-75 carries no DOI in the PubMed record, so the PubMed URL is cited). Registry results for NCT00987337 posted 2014-01-27 set the year.
efficacy.judgement: Scored contra by the letter of the rule: the replicon predicted an active genotype 1 antiviral and the sponsor's phase 2 primary endpoint (SVR) did not move. The miss is partial in substance: on-treatment virologic response did improve, as the replicon predicted, and the failure was relapse after a response-guided 24-week stop, which a replicon cannot model; the replicon had also flagged the single-substitution M423T barrier. Not neg: filibuvir's replicon potency (59-75 nM) was below dasabuvir's (2-8 nM) but no class bar exists for NNI potency, so the model's own data did not forecast failure. Tegobuvir, setrobuvir and lomibuvir were dropped without a published failed primary endpoint that I could verify in budget, so they are not scored. The track stays contra; a later tier 1-4 source showing the patient signal was background would be needed to turn it.

patient_trials.quote: SVR was achieved by 41.7, 39.6, and 45.8% of patients in the filibuvir 300 mg, 600 mg, and placebo arms, respectively.

efficacy.reason: Filibuvir add-on failed SVR; relapse unmodelled

efficacy.model: HCV-infected chimpanzee, 14-day NNI monotherapy (A-837093, dasabuvir's Abbott palm-I sibling)
efficacy.note: On 14-day sibling monotherapy both chimpanzees rebounded, selecting Y448H/G554D/D559G (GT1a) and C316Y/G554D (GT1b): a low barrier to NNI resistance; no patient outcome yet.
efficacy.quote: After this initial drop in the viral load, a rebound of plasma HCV RNA was observed in the genotype 1b-infected chimpanzee, while the genotype 1a-infected chimpanzee experienced a partial rebound that lasted throughout the treatment period.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 17908950). The substitution list (Y448H, G554D, D559G in GT1a; C316Y, G554D in GT1b) is the abstract's next sentence, 43 words, too long to quote whole.
efficacy.judgement: Opener on the chimpanzee track's efficacy cell, following the draft's convention of opening efficacy with the model's resistance-barrier prediction (the replicon's 2009 M423T opener): the chimpanzee predicted that NNI monotherapy gives a transient decline, then rebound with palm-site substitutions the replicon had also selected. Whether a resistance-pathway prediction scores in efficacy, engagement or neither is the checker's open rule question 4; placed here so the adjudicator can move the pair in one step.

efficacy.model: HCV-infected chimpanzee, 14-day NNI monotherapy (A-837093, dasabuvir's Abbott palm-I sibling)
efficacy.note: Dasabuvir-regimen failures in AVIATOR carried C316Y, and G554S/Y448H/D559G at the chimpanzee's other positions; the sibling's rebound substitutions were the drug's own clinical pathway.
efficacy.short: Chimp resistance sites emerged in patients
efficacy.quote: The most common variants in NS5B were M414T or M414I, S556G, and C316Y.
efficacy.confidence_note: MedR line 1291 read in the bundle text; the per-subtype treatment-emergent list (GT1a: G307R, C316Y, M414T, E446K/Q, A450V, A553T, G554S, S556G/R, G558R, D559G/I/N/V, Y561H, L588F; GT1b: C316Y, M414I, S556G) is MedR lines 3190-3192, and line 1294 says variants at M414, S556, G554 and Y448 persisted post-treatment. Patients were on the three-DAA regimen, not NNI monotherapy, so the chimpanzee's rebound-on-monotherapy prediction itself was never run in patients; what is compared is the substitution set. Krishnan 2015 (tier 1, epub 2015-06-22) carries the same AVIATOR data and is listed under patient_trials.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me (chimpanzee substitutions vs the FDA's list of treatment-emergent NS5B substitutions), comparison_stated false. Same, direction only: every position the chimpanzee selected on the sibling (316, 448, 554, 559) appears in dasabuvir-treated failures, with C316Y identical; the exact variants differ at 554 (G554D vs G554S) and the most prevalent patient variant, S556G, was not seen in the chimpanzee. Scored in efficacy on the draft's convention for resistance-pathway predictions; the primary-endpoint rule does not fit a resistance comparison, so endpoint_role is null and the adjudicator's answer to rule question 4 governs the cell. Year is the FDA review (Dec 2014); the AVIATOR registry posting followed on 2015-01-06.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: NS5B positions selected on sibling NNI monotherapy in chimpanzee vs treatment-emergent NS5B substitutions in dasabuvir-treated virologic failures

patient_trials.quote: The most prevalent treatment-emergent resistance-associated variants (RAVs) in GT1a were R155K and D168V in NS3, M28T and Q30R in NS5A, and S556G in NS5B.

efficacy.reason: Chimp sibling resistance sites recurred in patients

efficacy.model: Human-hepatocyte chimeric (uPA/SCID) mouse infected with patient-derived HCV, 4-week DAA mono- and combination therapy
efficacy.note: Sibling NNI BMS-821095 monotherapy broke through with resistant variants; NS5A inhibitor plus the NNI eradicated genotype 1b (not 2a/2b); no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: NS5A+NNI eradicates GT1b in chimeric mice
efficacy.quote: In contrast to monotherapy, 4 weeks of combination therapy with the NS5A RCI and either NS3 PI or NS5B inhibitor succeeded in completely eradicating the virus in genotype 1b HCV-infected mice.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed record PMID 23322441; Gut full text not fetched). Epub 2013-01-15, print Gut 62(7):1055-61. The abstract cites an earlier NS3+NS5B combination study in the same mice; whether that NS5B inhibitor was a non-nucleoside was not verified, so first use is dated to this paper.
efficacy.judgement: Opener for the chimeric-mouse track: the only in-vivo system in which HCV replicates in human hepatocytes and a DAA combination can be run to eradication, a different system with a different prediction (cure by combination, failure of monotherapy) from the replicon and the chimpanzee. The NNI was BMS-821095, a BMS sibling of beclabuvir, so product_in_model false. No regulator document in the bundle cites it.

efficacy.model: Human-hepatocyte chimeric (uPA/SCID) mouse infected with patient-derived HCV, 4-week DAA mono- and combination therapy
efficacy.note: Beclabuvir inside daclatasvir/asunaprevir/beclabuvir cured 87-98% (SVR12) of genotype 1 cirrhotics; the mouse's NS5A-plus-NNI eradication held, with an NS3 inhibitor added.
efficacy.quote: With the fixed-dose combination alone, response rates were 93% (97.5% CI, 85.4%-100.0%) for patients in the treatment-naive group and 87% (97.5% CI, 75.3%-98.0%) for those in the treatment-experienced group.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (JAMA 313(17):1736-44, PMID 25942724, published 2015-05-05). The trial regimen is three DAAs (NS5A + NS3 + NS5B NNI) where the mouse ran two-drug combinations, and 74% of patients were genotype 1a where the mouse's eradication was shown in 1b; the SVR12 split by subtype is in the body, not read. NCT01973049 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-05), so registry_date is null. UNITY-1 (non-cirrhotic) and the PMDA review were not verified in budget.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: the mouse's eradication with NS5A inhibitor + NNI (and failure of NNI monotherapy) against the first phase 3 of the only beclabuvir-containing regimen, whose primary endpoint SVR12 was met at 87-98%, so comparison_stated false and endpoint_role primary. Direction only: the regimen added asunaprevir to the mouse's pair, and the trial was mostly genotype 1a. Beclabuvir is a tile member (tiles.json), so it scores; the mouse was dosed with its sibling BMS-821095, product_in_model false. Year is the JAMA publication (May 2015); no registry results posting exists. The context note's 'only dasabuvir reached approval' is for the adjudicator; beclabuvir's replicon-track entry (Lemm 2014) belongs on the existing hcv-gt1-replicon track, not here.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: eradication in genotype 1b mice (NS5A inhibitor + NNI, 4 weeks) vs SVR12 in genotype 1 patients (74% GT1a) on a 12-week three-DAA regimen

patient_trials.quote: SVR12 rates were 98% (97.5% CI, 88.9%-100%) for patients in the treatment-naive group and 93% (97.5% CI, 85.0%-100.0%) for those in the treatment-experienced group when ribavirin was included in the regimen.

efficacy.model: Human-hepatocyte chimeric (uPA/SCID) mouse infected with patient-derived HCV, 4-week DAA mono- and combination therapy
efficacy.note: Mice carrying a DCV/ASV-failure patient's NS5A-L31V/Y93H virus relapsed (NS5B-P495S) after beclabuvir triple therapy; prior-DAA-failure patients mostly relapsed too; DAA-naive mouse and patient cured.
efficacy.short: Patient-virus mice forecast relapse in DAA failures
efficacy.quote: Sustained virological response was achieved in a DAA-naïve patient and one of the DCV/ASV treatment failures through DCV/ASV/BCV therapy; however, HCV relapse occurred in the other patients with prior DCV/ASV and/or sofosbuvir/ledipasvir treatment failures.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 29916799, J Gen Virol 99(8):1058-65, epub 2018-06-19; full text not read). Five patients, no registered trial, no pre-specified endpoint. Whether the serum donors were among the treated patients and whether the mice were dosed before the patients' outcomes were known is not stated in the abstract, so retrodiction is recorded false on the authors' framing (mouse result, then patients) and should be checked against the body.
efficacy.judgement: A patient-level use of the chimeric mouse with the product itself: mice infected with serum from a DCV/ASV failure carrying NS5A-L31V/Y93H relapsed with NS5B-P495S after 4 weeks of beclabuvir triple therapy, and the authors put that beside five patients treated with the same regimen, where most prior-DAA failures relapsed, so comparison_stated true and prediction_level patient. Partial, not full: one of the DCV/ASV failures did reach SVR, and the model's RAV (NS5B-P495S) is not reported for the patients in the abstract. Same with strengthens because the track already stood at same from 2015; endpoint_role null since a case series has no primary endpoint.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: relapse vs SVR after 12-week DCV/ASV/BCV: mice infected with patient serum vs the patients, by prior-DAA-failure status
efficacy.reason: Patient-virus mouse relapse matched DAA-failure relapse

safety.note: Animals showed no target organ at 10-120x clinical exposure; dasabuvir exposure tracked no anemia in patients, and ALT and bilirubin signals belong to paritaprevir.
safety.short: No animal target organ, none in patients
safety.quote: There was no association between ABT-333 or ritonavir exposures and reduction in hemoglobin levels in the multivariate logistic regression analysis.
safety.confidence_note: Both FDA reviews read in the bundle text. The univariate exposure-safety screen did list bilirubin and hemoglobin against ABT-333 exposure; the multivariate model attributed hemoglobin to ribavirin and bilirubin and ALT to ABT-450 (paritaprevir, OATP1B1). Component attribution inside a 3-DAA regimen is inferential, and the 2015 post-marketing hepatic-decompensation signal in cirrhotics is regimen-level and not attributable to dasabuvir.
safety.judgement: The animal package's stated prediction (no target organ, 10-120x margin) held: no dasabuvir-attributed harm appears in the label or the exposure-safety analysis, and the harms the regimen did show (ALT, bilirubin, anemia) are assigned to paritaprevir and ribavirin by the FDA reviewer. Paired by me (Pharmacology Review model side, Clinical Pharmacology Review patient side), so comparison_stated is false. Tegobuvir's 2007 phase 1 QT signal (Gilead press release, tier 5) would be a class safety entry if a preclinical hERG/ECG prediction could be found; none was in budget, so it is left unscored and named here.
